title: Automated Counterflow Centrifugal System for Small-Scale Cell Processing
protocol: Prepare buffers in a class 2 laminar flow hood.
Remove 50 mL of saline solution from a 500 mL saline bag using a syringe and needle assembly.
Replace the removed saline with 50 mL of 20% human serum albumin to make 2% HSA in saline as the wash buffer.
Remove cells from culture vessels for cell count determination by trypan blue exclusion.
Load counted cells into a transfer bag.
For adherent cells, add a digestion enzyme (e.g., trypsin) into the culture vessels to detach cells.
Quench with culture media once cells are detached.
Load cells into a transfer bag using a syringe and needle assembly.
Alternatively, cut the connecting tube with around 10 cm remaining attached to the transfer bag.
Add a female Luer connector to the end of the tubing.
Aspirate cells and media using a syringe.
Connect the syringe to the Luer connector.
Load cells into the transfer bag.
Connect the waste bag at position A.
Connect the wash buffer bag containing 500 mL of wash buffer at position B.
Connect the cell bag at positions D and F.
Connect the collecting syringe at position H.
Open the Graphic User Interface (GUI) of the device.
Press the "START" button on a laptop PC or tablet.
Open an existing protocol or press "New" to create a new one.
Use the "Forward" and "Backward" buttons to navigate through each step.
Select the valves to be opened/closed, centrifugal speed, pump speed, pump direction, and action triggers.
Save the protocol.
Place the single-use processing kit on the machine.
Hang the connected bags accordingly.
Press the red "Stop/Reset" button to reset all valves into the default closed position.
Connect the GUI to the processing device.
Press the "Connect" button.
Download the saved program.
Open the manual clamps for the transfer bag tubing.
Press the "Start" button to initiate the buffer exchange program.
Manually press the "Next" button to move to the next step before reaching the "Trigger".
Press the "Pause" button to halt the process and resume later if needed.
Check the status of valves J and K during recirculation.
Proceed to the next automation step when air in the bag triggers the bubble sensor.
Verify that the bag is empty before pressing "Next" or press "Pause" if triggered by a line bubble.
Close all tubing clamps when the automated process is finished.
Open the door and take the single-use kit out of the device.
Disconnect the syringe to collect the cells for subsequent processes.
Take a sample of the collected cells for a cell count and viability check.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 200 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 30 mL of cell wash buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension again at 200 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 10 mL of cell wash buffer.
Perform cell counting via the trypan blue exclusion assay to assess cell viability using an automated cell counter.
Perform an MTS assay to quantify cell proliferation at 2, 24, and 48 h.
Incubate each well containing 100 µL aliquot of cell culture media with 20 µL of MTS reagents for 2 h at 37 °C.
Assess the absorbance at 490 nm using a plate reader.
Perform functional assays to compare the impact of the automated process versus the manual process on the Jurkat cells and MSC function.
Culture Jurkat cells in a 96-well plate at a density of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Stimulate the cells with 50 ng/mL phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) and 1 µg/mL ionomycin in DMEM:F12 media containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Measure interleukin-2 production from culture supernatant using bead-based ELISA assay according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Culture mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in a 12-well plate at a density of 10,000 cells/cm² in DMEM:F12 media containing 10% FBS supplemented with interferon-γ at 50 units/mL.
Incubate the MSC cultures for 48 hours at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Collect supernatant from the MSC cultures for kynurenine concentration assay to measure indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) enzyme activity.
